summaries.demographer: Tyler Brizendine is a 69-year-old White, non-Hispanic divorced man living alone in a rented one-bedroom apartment in Austin's 78705 area (Q11, Q51-Q58, Q84-Q89). He was born in Waco, lived in Austin by age 16, and comes from a middle-class Central Texas household with two working parents and one younger sister (Q87, Q97-Q107). He has some college but no bachelor's degree and spent his career in telephone operations, now combining Social Security with part-time consulting income (Q65-Q74, Q90). His life-course profile shows stable work identity, post-divorce single living, close but non-cohabiting ties to an adult daughter, grandson, and sister (Q05-Q07).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Tyler is budget-conscious, loss-averse, and highly routine-oriented, tracking expenses in a spreadsheet and protecting a modest emergency fund (Q17, Q56-Q64, Q82-Q83). His choices show strong preference for stability over risk: he left college for dependable telephone work, avoids large debts, and limits discretionary spending when costs rise (Q02-Q04, Q60-Q64). He spends selectively on identity-rich experiences such as art, music, hiking, family meals, and planned travel rather than status goods (Q15, Q43, Q62). Peer routines, especially the walking group and family commitments, help him sustain health behaviors and social connection (Q15, Q31-Q32).
summaries.political_scientist: Tyler is a consistent voter and moderate-to-strong Democrat with fiscal caution rooted in older Texas norms (Q23-Q24, Q95-Q96). His civic orientation is local and procedural: he reads voter guides, values competent public programs, and focuses on housing, transit, health care, civil rights, and cultural preservation (Q23-Q25). He supports Black Lives Matter concerns around accountability and unequal treatment, has attended one local gathering, donated modestly, and adjusted art programming toward inclusion (Q26-Q30). He shows moderate institutional trust, relying on doctors and public health agencies while remaining wary of misinformation and political extremism (Q25, Q41-Q42).
summaries.psychologist: Tyler presents as conscientious, emotionally regulated, practical, and identity-anchored in usefulness, reliability, and calm communication (Q01-Q04, Q65, Q109). He copes with stress through organization, walking, cooking, reading, and social routines, while recognizing that he can hide hurt behind competence (Q43-Q45, Q50). His social style is warm but bounded: he lives alone, keeps regular but not constant contact with family, and maintains small purposeful circles through walking, art, volunteering, and former coworkers (Q05-Q07, Q11, Q15). Aging has prompted reflective adjustment rather than withdrawal, including reduced work hours, health maintenance, and hopes for independence, travel, family presence, and community contribution (Q18, Q31-Q33, Q108).
